introduction: On this Sunday, the prophet Elijah meets God not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire, but in a still small voice. In the Gospel, Jesus walks on the stormy sea; Peter walks toward him, begins to sink, and cries, Lord, save me! Jesus reaches out his hand. Paul speaks of his love for his own people. Let us listen for God's quiet voice and trust him in the storm.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord speaks peace to his people. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church, tossed by many storms: that she may keep her eyes fixed on Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are afraid and sinking under their troubles: that Jesus may stretch out his hand and save them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who seek God in silence and prayer: that they may hear his still small voice. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the Jewish people, to whom God first spoke: that God may bless them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that when our faith is weak, we may cry out, Lord, save me. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you speak to us in the silence and you reach out your hand when we are sinking. Strengthen our faith, and keep our eyes fixed on your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Lord, save me
reflection.body:
Elijah is exhausted and hiding in a cave on Mount Horeb. God tells him to go out and stand on the mountain, for the Lord is about to pass by. First comes a great wind that splits the rocks, "but the LORD was not in the wind." Then an earthquake, "but the LORD was not in the earthquake." Then a fire, "but the LORD was not in the fire." And then, "After the fire, there was a still small voice." Elijah covers his face and goes out. God often speaks not in the spectacular but in the quiet.

In the Gospel, Jesus sends his disciples ahead by boat while he goes up the mountain alone to pray. During the night, a storm rises and the boat is battered by the waves. Before dawn, Jesus comes to them, walking on the sea. They are terrified and think he is a ghost. He speaks to them: "Cheer up! It is I! Don't be afraid."

Peter, bold as ever, says, "Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters." Jesus says, "Come!" And Peter steps out of the boat and walks on the water. But "when he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, he cried out, saying," Lord, save me! Immediately Jesus reaches out his hand and catches him: "You of little faith, why did you doubt?"

Peter's story is ours. As long as he looked at Jesus, he walked on the water. When he looked at the wind, he sank. But even then, a short prayer was enough, and Jesus was there.

When they get into the boat, the wind stops, and the disciples worship him: "You are truly the Son of God!"

This week, make time for silence, and listen for God's quiet voice. And when the storms come, keep your eyes on Jesus. If you begin to sink, pray Peter's prayer: Lord, save me.
